description: "Team from CIn-UFPE developing climate-adaptive agricultural tools with NASA data."
summary: CIn the Stars is a cross-platform agricultural decision-support prototype designed to help farmers adapt to climate variability and compare crop-rotation strategies using NASA Earth-observation data. By querying NASA POWER climate records for local temperature and precipitation patterns, our explainable crop-ranking engine evaluates frost and water-demand thresholds alongside previous-crop nitrogen-fixation effects. We paired this climate-analysis engine with a React Native/Expo mobile interface for location-aware weather and scenario exploration, a FastAPI backend service, an exploratory LangGraph AI assistant, and a YOLOv8 plant-health computer-vision pipeline. CIn the Stars bridges the gap between complex satellite-derived agro-climatic datasets and accessible, transparent field-level planting decisions to strengthen soil resilience and food security.
details:
What It Does & How It Works

CIn the Stars is an agricultural decision-support prototype designed to help farmers navigate shifting temperatures, erratic rainfall, and soil degradation. Instead of operating as a black-box recommender, our system combines NASA Earth-observation climate records with transparent agronomic logic across five modular components:

1. Climate & Crop-Rotation Engine (Python, Pandas, NumPy): Queries the NASA POWER daily point API (T2M_MIN and PRECTOTCORR) for user-specified coordinates and evaluates an agronomic crop matrix using frost thresholds, water-demand classifications, and previous-crop nitrogen-fixation adjustments. Our exploratory notebooks also analyze multi-year (2021–2025) NASA POWER variables—including T2M, T2M_MAX, RH2M, and GWETROOT—across contrasting agricultural biomes (Petrolina in Brazil, Niamey in Niger, and Cherkasy in Ukraine).

2. Cross-Platform Mobile Application (React Native, Expo, TypeScript): Provides an accessible field interface featuring device geolocation, real-time weather visualization, agricultural profile management, crop-rotation scenario comparisons, and camera/chat screens.

3. Weather API Service (FastAPI, Pydantic, HTTPX): Implements validated REST endpoints (GET /api/weather/current) that normalize real-time meteorological conditions for the mobile client.

4. AI-Agent Workflow Experiment (LangGraph, LangChain, Groq): Prototypes a conversational routing graph that ingests deterministic outputs from the crop-rotation engine to translate technical scores into plain-language agronomic guidance.

5. Plant Health Computer-Vision Pipeline (Ultralytics YOLOv8, PyTorch, OpenCV): Includes dataset auditing, preparation, and YOLOv8 image-classification training/evaluation scripts built on PlantVillage data to support future leaf-disease screening.

Benefits, Creativity & Factors Considered

- Explainability & Trust: Farmers can inspect the exact climate filters and rotation benefits behind each crop ranking rather than blindly trusting an opaque score.

- Key Agronomic & Environmental Factors: Frost tolerance, seasonal precipitation availability, crop water demand, nitrogen-fixing rotational benefits, and local real-time weather conditions.

- Transparency in Prototype Scope: We clearly distinguish production-ready components (real-time weather backend and NASA POWER rotation engine) from demonstration UI scenarios and experimental AI/vision pipelines.

Intended Impact

By bridging raw satellite/reanalysis climate datasets with intuitive mobile decision-support tools, CIn the Stars empowers smallholder and regional farmers to plan resilient crop rotations, conserve water, protect soil health, and adapt proactively to climate variability.
